content:
maya: FYI — Acme (enterprise) asked for per-org routing overrides so all /v1/generate traffic goes to their dedicated cluster. They want header overrides + a fallback to hosted if capacity low. Need quick design + risk checklist.

sam: Do they want every path or only specific endpoints?

maya: Only generation and chat endpoints for now: /v1/generate, /v1/chat. Also want a static header set for auditing: X-Redwood-Org-Route: acme-dedicated.

liam: Suggested config shape (proto):
```json
{
  "org_id": "org_54321",
  "routes": [
    {
      "match": { "path_prefix": "/v1/generate", "method": "POST" },
      "action": { "backend": "dedicated-us-west-2", "force_model": "rwd-4x-dedicated" },
      "headers": { "x-routing-reason": "enterprise-exception" }
    }
  ],
  "allowlist": ["10.1.2.0/24", "34.56.78.9"],
  "denylist": []
}
```
This gives explicit match -> backend mapping + header injection and network allowlist.

jess: A few things to call out: precedence rules (global routing -> org overrides -> route-specific) need to be explicit. Also denylist should supersede allowlist? I'd prefer denylist > allowlist > org override (fail closed).

dan: We also need audit logs for any override decision and a metric tag like routing.override=org_54321 to track cost. Also add a safety TTL on overrides so they expire unless renewed.

sam: Edge cases: what if their dedicated pool is out of capacity? They said fallback to hosted is okay but only if they opt-in. We need an opt-in flag per-org and a circuit breaker that flips if latency/SLOs degrade.

liam: Implementation notes: Gateway rule engine needs to evaluate in this order: 1) IP denylist check; 2) org-level explicit deny; 3) route match (path/method/header); 4) allowlist check; 5) backend choice. We should implement a short-circuit evaluation and emit a decision log for each request.

jess: UI/UX: Console needs an 'Enterprise Exceptions' editor with: org selector, route matcher builder, header injector, network allow/deny, TTL + owner, and a preview/simulate button that runs a sample path against rules. Permissions: only account admins + platform-admin can add.

maya: Ops questions — who owns rollout? Can we ship a minimal beta with feature-flagged support and no UI (yaml only) so SRE + SEs can test?

dan: I'll own the beta rollout and add telemetry. plan: feature flag behind ff/org-routing-exceptions, start with 3 customers, monitor routing.override.* metrics and token/hour delta.

ops-bot: deploybot: feature flag ff/org-routing-exceptions created in staging.

sam: Security note: header injection must be signed or write-only so customers can't spoof. Use a signed header pattern: X-Redwood-Org-Sig and validate in gateway.

liam: Agreed. Implementation checklist I'll pick up: rule schema + evaluator + decision-logs + TTL enforcement + signature validation. Estimate: 2 sprints to beta (feature-flagged, yaml only).

maya: Action items:
- liam: RFC + schema PR by EOD Wed
- dan: telemetry + audit log schema by Fri
- jess: console wireframes for next week (if we go GA)
- sam: threat model checklist (security)

maya: Thanks — this is higher priority because Acme is on our enterprise onboarding path. Will update when RFC lands. :eyes:
